collections.title: Games for a five-minute break
collections.description: Browser games we would open when there are only a few minutes left: quick to load, quick to understand, and easy to leave.
intro: This is not a ranking of the best games in the catalogue. It is a practical short-session list: games that give you a complete little decision in roughly two to five minutes, without a long tutorial or a save file you have to protect.

The session labels are editor estimates, not measured playtimes. We combine the publisher's description, the control scheme and our own notes. If a game has a longer progression layer, it belongs in a different collection.
criteria: The first screen explains the objective without a long tutorial.
No account or download; closing the tab is a clean exit.
A clear round, score or short objective rather than a multi-hour campaign.

collections.title: Two players, one screen
collections.description: Games for a second person in the room, a shared keyboard, or a friend in a lobby. Each entry says which kind of two-player mode it actually is.
intro: “Two player” is not one mode. Some games put both players on the same keyboard; some pass one mouse back and forth; others are online matches that need another person in a lobby. This collection separates those cases instead of pretending they are the same.

Read the note under each pick before inviting someone. If a page says the publisher did not list controls, treat the first screen as the tutorial. A local game with no second player is not a local game.
criteria: Supports at least two players in a local, pass-and-play or online mode.
The mode is stated by the publisher or visible on the game page.
We separate same-keyboard, shared-screen and online play.
No account required for the local picks.

collections.title: Free Chromebook games with no download
collections.description: Light browser games whose embeds declare a mobile viewport and a small initial payload. School networks can still block hosts.
intro: A Chromebook runs the browser as its operating system, so the useful question is not whether there is a ChromeOS version, but whether this free embed loads without a heavy client and fits a small screen.

These picks passed two static checks: the embed declares a viewport and the initial HTML plus linked runtime was under 1 MB in our cold-fetch test. That is not a promise that a managed school network will allow the host, and it is not a frame-rate measurement. Check the load-time index for the raw numbers.
criteria: Initial payload under 1 MB in the cold-fetch test.
A short or medium session, so a shared device is not tied up for long.

collections.title: Games with no save-file pressure
collections.description: Short runs and score chases where closing the tab does not cost you a carefully built save. Good for waiting rooms, queues and five-minute gaps.
intro: Some games are relaxing until you remember the save file. This collection is the opposite: rounds reset, scores are disposable, and leaving early is a normal way to stop.

These are not all “easy” games. Some are frantic and competitive. The shared property is that the session is the unit, not a campaign you have to protect. If a game has meta-progression, it is not in this list.
criteria: No campaign save that is lost when you close the tab.
Leaving mid-run is an expected action.
No account or cloud save required.
